# The Watchman of the Autumn Sky

## Scripture

**"He spreads out the northern skies over empty space; he suspends the earth over nothing." — Job 26:7 (NIV)**

## Reflection

On crisp September evenings, a faint band of light arcs overhead—the Milky Way, our galaxy seen edge-on. Ancient travelers called it the "Backbone of Night," a river of stars guiding their way. What strikes me most is how *still* it all is. No pillars hold it up. No cables suspend it. It simply hangs there, silent and sure, as it has for ages.

Job wrote of this long before telescopes or satellites. He looked up and saw a God who "spreads out the northern skies over empty space." No scaffolding. No safety net. Just the word of a faithful Creator holding everything in place.

Autumn reminds us that seasons change. Leaves fall. Light fades earlier each evening. Yet the northern skies stay faithful—the same constellations our grandparents knew, the same stars Abraham counted. God's creation isn't fragile or frantic; it rests on His character.

Maybe you feel like the earth beneath you is "over nothing" right now—a job uncertain, a relationship shifting, a future unclear. The God who suspends galaxies without visible support can hold your life too. He doesn't need your circumstances to be stable to keep you steady. He simply speaks, and it holds.

Tonight, step outside. Let the quiet sky remind you: what looks unsupported is actually upheld by nail-scarred hands.

## Prayer

Father, when my life feels suspended over nothing, remind me that You hold all things together. Thank You for the silent, faithful witness of the autumn sky. Teach me to trust Your word more than my circumstances. In Jesus' name, Amen.
